description: language_is_empty checks if any accepting state is reachable from start by treating NFA as directed graph. Builds graph from delta (ignoring symbols), runs DFS with stack. Three test NFAs: ends-in-ab (not empty), dead-accept (accept unreachable, empty), accepts-epsilon (start is accepting, not empty).

steps.description: Purpose: determine if NFA language is empty by checking reachability of accepting states from start.

language_is_empty: builds graph dict from delta (lines 9-10) by collecting all destinations per source, ignoring symbols. DFS: visited set, stack initialized with start states. Loop pops node, skips if visited, adds to visited, checks if in accept (return False = not empty), pushes unvisited neighbors. Returns True if stack exhausted without finding accept.
Early exit: if node in accept, immediately return False. Language is NOT empty because an accepting state is reachable.

steps.answer: Emptiness only cares whether ANY path reaches an accept state, not which string labels that path. Symbols are irrelevant to reachability.
steps.question: Why does the graph construction ignore transition symbols?

steps.description: Three test NFAs: ENDS_IN_AB (q0->q1->q2 reachable, not empty); DEAD_ACCEPT (s0->s1 only, s2 never reached, empty); ACCEPTS_EPSILON (start q0 is accepting, not empty, accepts empty string).
Output: ends-in-ab empty? False; dead-accept empty? True; accepts-epsilon empty? False.

title: Language Emptiness via DFS Reachability on NFA
